requisitions.title: Senior Frontend Engineer
requisitions.description:
## About Acme
Acme is building the next generation of AI-powered developer tools. Our platform helps engineering teams ship faster with intelligent code assistance, automated testing, and real-time collaboration. Backed by top-tier investors, we're growing rapidly and looking for exceptional people to join us.

## About the role
We're looking for a Senior Frontend Engineer to lead the development of our core product interfaces. You'll work closely with design and product to craft polished, performant experiences used by thousands of developers every day. This is a high-impact role where you'll shape both the technical architecture and the user experience of our flagship products.

## What you'll do
- Own the frontend architecture for our main web application, built with React and TypeScript
- Collaborate with designers to translate Figma specs into pixel-perfect, accessible components
- Build and maintain a shared component library used across multiple product surfaces
- Drive performance improvements and establish frontend best practices
- Mentor junior engineers and contribute to technical design reviews
- Partner with backend engineers to define API contracts and data models
requirements: 5+ years of professional frontend development experience
Deep expertise in React, TypeScript, and modern CSS (Tailwind preferred)
Experience building and maintaining design systems or component libraries
Strong understanding of web performance, accessibility, and responsive design
Excellent communication skills and experience working in cross-functional teams
Experience with testing frameworks (Vitest, Playwright, or similar)
assessment_criteria: 5+ years of professional frontend development experience
Deep expertise in React, TypeScript, and modern CSS
Experience building design systems or component libraries
Strong understanding of web performance and accessibility
Experience mentoring engineers or leading technical initiatives

requisitions.title: Machine Learning Engineer
requisitions.description:
## About Acme
Acme is building the next generation of AI-powered developer tools. Our platform helps engineering teams ship faster with intelligent code assistance, automated testing, and real-time collaboration. Backed by top-tier investors, we're growing rapidly and looking for exceptional people to join us.

## About the role
We're hiring a Machine Learning Engineer to work on the core AI models that power our product. You'll develop and optimize large language models for code understanding, generation, and review. This role sits at the intersection of ML research and production engineering — you'll prototype new model architectures and ship them to thousands of users.

## What you'll do
- Train, fine-tune, and evaluate LLMs for code-related tasks
- Build robust ML pipelines for data processing, training, and inference at scale
- Collaborate with product teams to translate user needs into model capabilities
- Optimize model performance for latency, cost, and quality
- Stay current with the latest ML research and identify techniques applicable to our domain
- Contribute to our evaluation frameworks and experimentation infrastructure
requirements: 3+ years of experience in machine learning engineering or applied ML research
Hands-on experience with LLMs — fine-tuning, RLHF, prompt engineering, or inference optimization
Proficiency in Python, PyTorch, and distributed training frameworks
Experience building production ML systems with monitoring and observability
Strong fundamentals in statistics, linear algebra, and optimization
Published research or meaningful open-source contributions in ML are a plus
assessment_criteria: 3+ years of ML engineering or applied ML research experience
Hands-on experience with LLMs including fine-tuning or inference optimization
Proficiency in Python, PyTorch, and distributed training frameworks
Experience building production ML systems with monitoring
Strong fundamentals in statistics and optimization

intakes.title: Product Designer
intakes.content:
Role overview

We're hiring a Product Designer to own the end-to-end design of a core surface in our product. You'll partner closely with a PM and an EM, drive design from research through ship, and raise the bar on craft across the team.

Team: Growth · Reports to: Head of Design · Level: IC4–IC5 · Location: SF or remote (US)

Why this role exists

Our growth surface drives a meaningful share of activation, but the experience has grown faster than its design system. We need a senior designer who can hold the whole journey in their head, simplify it, and ship.

What you'll do

  • Lead design for the growth funnel — onboarding, activation, and the first 7 days
  • Run lightweight research: usability tests, in-app prompts, and qual interviews
  • Define and evolve patterns in our design system in partnership with the systems team
  • Prototype to communicate — static mocks are the floor, not the ceiling
  • Collaborate daily with PM and engineering from kickoff through QA

What we're looking for

Must-haves

  • 5+ years designing consumer or prosumer software, ideally at a product-led company
  • A portfolio showing shipped work with measurable outcomes, not just artifacts
  • Strong interaction craft: hierarchy, motion, copy, edge cases
  • Comfort with ambiguity — you can scope a vague problem into shippable bets

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience designing for growth, onboarding, or experimentation surfaces
  • Fluency in Figma variables, auto-layout, and component APIs
  • Background in front-end engineering or prototyping in code

Success in 90 days

  1. Mapped the current onboarding flow and shipped one high-confidence simplification
  2. Established a recurring design review cadence with PM and engineering
  3. Contributed at least two reusable patterns back to the design system

Compensation & logistics

  • Salary band: $180k–$220k base + equity
  • Employment type: Full-time
  • Interview loop: Recruiter screen → hiring manager → portfolio review → design exercise → cross-functional panel
Strong preference for candidates who can show their thinking, not just their pixels. We'll dig into trade-offs and what got cut.
